result:
Revisit check: no Revisit dates have passed. The nearest is bake-to-order on 2026-12-02.

I've left out the free first box. You dropped it on 2026-10-06 because only 6 of 52 people went on to pay, and the free boxes took Saturday slots from paying customers. You said you'd look at it again only if paid signups fell below 8 a month for 2 months in a row. October had 15, so that hasn't happened. "Flat" is still well above that line.

Here are 3 ideas that work within your capacity limits:

**1. Referral from current subscribers: half price for the friend, a free loaf for the referrer**
You discarded 50% off the first month, but you said you'd reopen it if it came through a referral from an existing subscriber. This is that test. Each of your 140 subscribers gets a code. A friend who uses it pays €9 a week for their first month, and the referrer gets a pastry or loaf added to their next box. People who come recommended by a neighbour are much more likely to stay than people chasing a free box. Run it for 6 weeks and compare conversion with the 6/52 from September. Cost: printed cards in every box (about €40) plus the discount, which you only give on actual signups.

**2. "Building drops": sign up together for one delivery stop**
Ask subscribers if neighbours in their building or street would join. Once 3 or more households at one address sign up, they share a single delivery stop. Give them a small reason to organise it, such as a free seasonal loaf for the group each month. This adds subscribers without using more Saturday slots, which is your real limit. It also fits your own cargo bike delivery. Cost: close to zero, plus a flyer for subscribers to put in their building's hallway.

**3. Tastings in the shop with on-the-spot signup**
On your busiest walk-in days, give out tasting pieces of this week's box loaves at the counter. Put up a QR code and a card that says "this Saturday's box" so people can subscribe right there. This isn't café seating or surplus stock, because the tasting bread comes out of the bake you're already doing to order. It reaches people who already like your shop but haven't subscribed. Cost: about €20–30 a week in bread, which fits your €300 budget.

My recommendation is to start with #1. It gives you a clean, logged test of the one discount you said you'd reconsider, and your existing subscribers are your cheapest channel.

If you choose one of these, tell me and I'll log it in the ledger.
